headline: GOLD BULLION ETFs ABSORB $6.4B IN ONE WEEK — LARGEST INFLOW IN 10 MONTHS AS PCE AND WARSH SPEECH LOOM
snippet: Gold-backed ETFs absorbed 47 tonnes ($6.4 billion) in the past week — the largest single-week inflow in approximately 10 months — as gold held near $4,663 on Tuesday ahead of two critical catalysts: Wednesday's core PCE print (consensus 0.2% MoM, with 0.3%+ seen as the threshold for renewed rate-hike bets) and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's debut Jackson Hole keynote Friday morning. A hotter-than-expected PCE is the primary short-term risk to the rally.

headline: U.S. DEPT OF WAR ANCHORS $750M INTO USAR RARE EARTH VEHICLE — ONLY NON-ASIAN MAGNETIC REE PRODUCER GOES TO SHAREHOLDER VOTE AUG 28
snippet: USA Rare Earth completed a $1.55 billion capitalization of its government-backed special purpose vehicle to purchase 100% of Serra Verde's Phase 1 rare earth output. The Department of War committed $750M (up from an original $500M), a tier-1 bank provided a $500M revolving credit facility, and the U.S. government signed a $300M five-year forward purchase contract. Serra Verde's Pela Ema mine in Brazil is the only operation outside Asia currently producing all four magnetic rare earth elements — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium — at commercial scale. The $2.83 billion acquisition vote is scheduled for August 28.

headline: BHP IN URANIUM TALKS WITH NEXGEN ENERGY — ROOK I COMBO WOULD FORGE WORLD'S LARGEST U3O8 PRODUCER
snippet: BHP Group is in exploratory discussions with NexGen Energy over its Rook I project in Saskatchewan, which holds 25 million pounds of annual uranium production capacity. Combined with BHP's Olympic Dam at 10 million pounds per year, a deal would create the world's largest uranium producer by output. The talks arrive as uranium spot climbed to $89.50/lb — a 6-month high — and NexGen speculation has driven two consecutive weekly gains for the stock. BHP has not confirmed a formal bid.

headline: KAZATOMPROM SLASHES 2026 URANIUM OUTPUT BY 8M LBS — SULPHURIC ACID PLANT SUSPENDED AFTER FOSSIL DISCOVERY
snippet: Kazakhstan's Kazatomprom announced plans to cut 2026 uranium production from 32,777 to 29,697 metric tonnes U3O8, removing roughly 8 million pounds — approximately 5% of global annual supply — from the market. A secondary disruption: construction of a critical sulphuric acid plant was suspended after palaeontological specimens were found at the site, requiring official permits before work can resume. Uranium spot responded by climbing to $89.50/lb, its highest level in six months.

headline: NEVGOLD DRILLS 50.3m OF 1.38 g/t AuEq AT LIMOUSINE BUTTE — FIRST 2026 HOLES EXTEND MRE 100m OUTSIDE BLOCK MODEL
snippet: NevGold's first three 2026 drillholes at Limousine Butte in Nevada intersected significant antimony-gold mineralization 100 metres outside the existing block model, including 1.38 g/t AuEq over 50.3 metres from surface — a zone containing 1.16% antimony over 3.0 metres. The shallow, 100% oxide deposit is a heap-leach candidate, and antimony's designation as a U.S. Department of Defense critical mineral adds strategic value. NevGold is targeting a 20,000-metre 2026 drill program to drive resource expansion ahead of a near-term production decision.

headline: TRAFIGURA DRIVES 20,000t SINGLE-DAY LME COPPER SURGE — BIGGEST WAREHOUSE BUILD SINCE APRIL AS BIDDING WAR LOOMS
snippet: LME copper inventories surged 20,000 tonnes in a single session — the largest single-day build since April — with Trafigura Group reportedly responsible for a substantial portion of the inflows. The move brings LME stocks to 238,575 tonnes, still well below year-ago levels but representing a notable shift from the 42-session consecutive drawdown seen earlier in 2026. Copper held near $6.61/lb ($14,100/t), with traders now watching for a London warehouse bidding war that could reignite the squeeze that pushed COMEX to its all-time record of $6.7270/lb earlier this month.

headline: MINERAL RESOURCES FY26: RECORD 341Mt PRODUCTION, A$490M MT MARION EXPANSION APPROVED WITH GANFENG
snippet: Mineral Resources posted record FY2026 production of 341 million tonnes, up 22% year on year, with attributable spodumene sales reaching a record 158,000 dmt SC6 at an average realised price of US$2,425/dmt — up 15% quarter on quarter. The company simultaneously approved a A$490 million expansion of its Mt Marion lithium mine in a 100% joint venture with Ganfeng, targeting first Bald Hill shipments from the Port of Esperance in Q1 FY27. Net debt fell to AUD 4.3 billion with liquidity of AUD 2.4 billion.

headline: LITHIUM HITS 5-MONTH LOW AT 157,000 CNY/T — BALD HILL AND FINNISS RESTARTS STOKE 2027 OVERSUPPLY FEARS
snippet: Lithium carbonate fell to 157,000 CNY/T on August 25, its lowest level in five months, as the reactivation of Mineral Resources' Bald Hill and Core Lithium's Finniss operations begins to add new supply into a market analysts are starting to model as oversupplied in 2027. The price declined 2.18% in a single session as investors weighed whether the recovery in producer economics — which triggered the restart wave in the first place — can survive the volume increase those restarts bring.

headline: JACKSON HOLE 2026: THREE SCENARIOS FOR WARSH AND THE GOLD MARKET — WHY THE METAL MAY WIN UNDER EACH
snippet: With Fed Chair Kevin Warsh set to deliver his debut Jackson Hole address Friday, analysis maps three rate scenarios — dovish pivot, extended hold, surprise hawkish signal — and argues gold's ongoing debasement-driven rally has structurally decoupled from the traditional rate-sensitivity framework. The thesis: gold is now pricing in fiscal risk and dollar debasement rather than rate risk, meaning even a hawkish Warsh may not sustainably reverse the bull as long as Treasury buyback programs expand and the deficit trajectory remains unchecked.

headline: ABITIBI METALS ACHIEVES 98.2% COPPER RECOVERY AT B26 — 23.7% Cu CONCENTRATE IN FIRST METALLURGICAL TESTWORK
snippet: Abitibi Metals reported best-in-class initial metallurgical recoveries from the B26 polymetallic VMS deposit in Quebec, with laboratory-scale testing achieving 98.2% copper recovery into a saleable concentrate grading 23.7% Cu. The results significantly de-risk the extraction economics of the project, which is being drilled by three active rigs on a 40,000-metre program. High copper recovery into a clean concentrate is a critical threshold for VMS development decisions.
